claims.claim: Gessey-Jones and colleagues found the distribution of intervals between significant deaths measured in chapters to be geometric rather than power law.
Gessey-Jones and colleagues counted two characters as interacting if they directly meet or the text makes it explicitly clear they knew one another.
claims.quote: if they directly meet each other or it is explicitly

claims.claim: Riggs reports that Carroll's main thrust is that Martin uses an argument from authenticity to justify his treatment of women, violence and non-Westerosi characters.
claims.source: Don Riggs, book review, Fafnir 6.2 (2019), reporting Shiloh Carroll

claims.claim: Carroll characterises Martin's way of reimagining the Middle Ages as violent, dark, brutal, and relentlessly masculine.
claims.quote: violent, dark, brutal, and relentlessly masculine

claims.claim: Carroll quotes Martin's defence that it is fundamentally dishonest to write a war story and leave rape out.
claims.source: George R. R. Martin, quoted by Shiloh Carroll, The Public Medievalist (2018)
claims.quote: if you write a war story and you leave that out
claims.page: section 'A Savage Beast in Every Man'

claims.quote: forcing the author to describe and explain what

claims.claim: Acree reports that García and Antonsson pored over 10,000 pages of novels, pulling out all references to history, myths and legends, before Martin filled in the blanks.
claims.source: Cat Acree, BookPage interview feature, December 2014
claims.quote: pored over 10,000 pages of novels, pulling out all references to history

claims.quote: I was supposed to write 50,000 words of text for sidebars

claims.claim: Germani describes Martin as setting his narrative atop an iceberg of history and using that background to give the text solidity.

claims.quote: setting your narrative atop this iceberg of history

claims.feature: other: prior life of the cast
claims.claim: Germani writes that part of why Martin's world feels lived-in is that everyone had a life before page one.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Now, As We All Know', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: Everyone had a life before page one

claims.claim: Germani argues Martin keeps readers turning pages with a steady flow of low-density sentences.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'George R.R. Martin, The American Homer', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: Martin keeps us turning pages with a steady flow of low-density sentences

claims.claim: Germani writes that most fantasists settle for a few linguistic relics to give a historical veneer, and names 'must needs', 'soon or late' and 'near as' among Martin's.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Linguistic Anachronism', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: a few linguistic relics to give a historical veneer

claims.claim: Germani argues that what a fantasy writer needs to build is cultures rather than worlds, and that a culture is before anything else a language and a voice.
claims.source: Erik Germani, 'Linguistic Anachronism', At Sea Journal
claims.quote: What we need to do is build cultures, not worlds
